content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain dry spaghetti are pasta made from whole wheat flour, retaining the bran and germ. This makes them more nutritious than regular white spaghetti, with a nutty aroma and a slightly firmer bite after cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains about twice the fiber of traditional white pasta.
Spaghetti were first documented in Italy in the 13th century.
When cooking whole grain spaghetti, a little extra water helps prevent sticking.
Whole grains preserve more B‑vitamins and minerals such as magnesium and iron.
In some countries whole grain pasta is called "integrale" or "whole wheat".

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B3 aid energy metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Magnesium and iron are important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white pasta, whole grain pasta raises blood glucose more slowly, which can aid weight management.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Plant antioxidants and phytosterols may help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat pasta contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Like all carbohydrate foods, excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Some brands add preservatives; check the ingredient list if you have allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water for 8–12 minutes until al dente, then serve with sauces, vegetables, seafood or meat. It can also be used in casseroles, cold pasta salads, or as a base for pasta bowls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry spaghetti in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to an airtight jar to protect from moisture and pests.
